summary: (e) BYPL and BRPL are no longer necessary or proper parties in the present Petition and hence ought to be deleted from the array of parties. Arraying the said Respondents in the present proceedings was not necessitated on account of any direct legal interest but rather at the insistence of SECI’s back-to-back contractual arrangements with the said Distribution Companies. Presently, in the absence of any subsisting contractual relationships, BYPL and BRPL cannot be considered as necessary or proper parties to the present adjudication. (n) During the construction phase of the project, the Petitioners have taken the benefit of the underlying contract with BYPL and BRPL. In fact, even while seeking various permissions and linkages, the Petitioners, throughout, called out to the PPA and the connected PSA with BRPL and BYPL. The Petitioners cannot be permitted to take a contrary approach at their convenience, where on the one hand, they have taken the benefit of the relationship with the BYPL and BRPL, and on the other hand, they choose to de-tag themselves from BRPL and BYPL. _SCC 417]_ is entirely misplaced. The Petitioners have placed reliance on the observation of the Hon’ble Supreme Court that _“the fact that a person is likely to secure a right/ interest in a lis, after the lis is decided, will not make such person a necessary party or a proper party to same”._ However, this observation is not applicable to the present dispute. In fact, the situation is the reverse in the present case because BRPL and BYPL continue to have a right/ interest in the present dispute. It is not the case that BRPL and BYPL are ‘likely’ to have such a right/ interest, as alleged by the Petitioners. 9. The Petition, along with IA No. 61/2025, was listed for the hearing on 19.8.2025. The Petitioners made detailed submissions in the matter with respect to the deletion of BYPL and BRPL from the array of parties. The same was objected to by BYPL and BRPL. On the request of Petitioners and the Respondents, BYPL and BRPL, the Commission permitted the Petitioners and Respondents, BRPL and BYPL, to file their respective written submissions in IA No. 61 of 2025, and the order was reserved in IA No. 61 of 2025. The Petitioners and Respondents have filed their written submissions in this regard, which are not repeated here for the sake of brevity. 10. The gravamen of the issue involved in the present IA pertains to the deletion of the names of the Respondents, BYPL and BRPL, from the array of parties. The Petitioners have vehemently argued that BRPL and BYPL are neither necessary nor proper parties to the present Petition and, therefore, they ought to be removed from the array of Respondents. Whereas, the Respondents, BRPL and BYPL, while _vehemently_ contesting the said submissions, have argued that they continue to be necessary and proper parties to the Petition. 12. On the contrary, it is the Respondents’ case that they are necessary and proper parties in Petition No. 91/MP/2024. In fact, the Petitioners themselves have added BRPL and BYPL as parties at the time of the filing of the Petition and now, at Petitioners. We note that the Petition has been filed on 6.2.2024 by the Petitioners seeking in-principle approval of certain events, Change in Law, and for an appropriate mechanism for appropriate adjustment/ compensation to offset the financial/ commercial impact of the Change in Law events in terms of the PPA between Petitioners and SECI. _— (2) Court may strike out or add parties._ _ The Court may at any stage of the proceedings, either upon or without the application of either party, _ _ and on such terms as may appear to the Court to be just, order that the name of any party improperly joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, be struck out, and that the name of any person who ought to have been joined, whether as plaintiff or defendant, or whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the suit, be added. _ 17. For the purpose of answering the pivotal question at hand, we only need to refer to Sub-rule (2) of Order I Rule 10. A bare reading of the provision extracted above indicates that Sub-rule (2) vests a very broad and substantial power in the court to delete or add a party, at any stage of the suit proceedings, either _suo motu_ or upon an application of either of the parties before it. It provides that the court may delete the name of a party on such terms as may appear to the court to be just and proper. It may add any party whose presence before the court is necessary for the effective and complete adjudication of the dispute. _“24. Under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Civil Procedure Code the court has the power to pass orders regarding the adding of parties or striking off the name of a party. Whether the exercise of this power is a matter of jurisdiction or of discretion appears to have been the subject of difference of opinion in the_ 22. Applying such observations to the present matter, we note that BRPL and BYPL at the present stage do not hold any right at present in Petition No. 91/MP/2024 since they no longer have a valid arrangement for the procurement of power from the Petitioners’ solar power projects. We also note that when the Petition was filed before the Commission, the Respondents had a substantial interest in the outcome of the Change in Law proceedings as they had a valid existing PSA with SECI; however, after the termination of their PSA, during the pendency of proceedings before us, they no longer can be said to have any direct or substantial interest in the outcome of Change in Law proceedings. Merely on the ground that their right/ interest in the PSA may be revived in future after the outcome of a challenge laid before the DERC, the Respondents at this stage cannot be considered as a necessary or a proper party in the Petition.
